text:
nina: heads-up — seeing a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on chat-prod starting ~04:20 UTC
omar: how big of a drop?
tess: also noticed p95 jitter around the same time window
nina: route chat.realtime: baseline ~88% -> ~80% hit-rate, p95 up ~40ms
metrics-bot: deploys around that time: prompt-sanitizer v2.9.0 @04:12, kernel-batcher v3.4.1 @04:15, keyer-lib v1.2.0 @03:50
joel: sample sanitized cache key?
nina: `ck:v3|tok=tok-2026-03|sys=assistant_v2|pref=What's the ETA on my order?|tools={format:json,search:true}`
joel: tools map looks insertion-ordered — could be nondeterministic and cause different hashes
tess: we also changed whitespace normalization in prompt-sanitizer yesterday; small punctuation trimming
omar: flamegraph/traces from 04:10-04:30 show backend.tokenize spikes and more KV lookups
nina: histogramed tool-arg permutations across 1h: ~4-5% of requests have same logical tools but different literal ordering -> likely ~3-5% hit loss
joel: aligns with 88->80 delta. Also kernel-batcher tweak could have reduced opportunistic batching -> fewer warmup hits
tess: quick mitigation idea: add a read-side tolerant probe that computes an alternate key with sorted tool keys and probes after primary miss (reads only, no writes)
omar: low risk. need metrics: cache.tolerant_read and cache.tolerant_hit
joel: patch plan: compute alternate_key = key_with_sorted_tools; if primary_miss then probe alternate_key and emit tolerant metrics; do not write using alternate key
nina: also hotfix promptlib: stableSerialize(obj) using sorted keys + trimmed whitespace for system prompt
tess: I'll add a CI unit test that permutes map order and asserts stableSerialize invariance
metrics-bot: perf snapshot 04:00-04:10 vs 04:20-04:30:
```:route chat.realtime
p50 20ms -> 24ms
p95 110ms -> 150ms
cache_hit_rate 0.88 -> 0.80
warmup_miss_ratio +0.05
```
omar: implement tolerant_read behind a feature flag and canary 10%
joel: also add debug `cache.key.parts` logging on canary: (hash_src, tok_ver, promptlib_ver, tools_sorted_flag)
nina: ownership:
- joel: implement tolerant_read (1h) + logs
- tess: promptlib stableSerialize PR + CI test
- omar: microbenchmark kernel-batcher v3.4.0 vs v3.4.1 for merge window timings
- nina: run 24h key-diff audit and prepare incident note
metrics-bot: canary started for kv-tolerant-read @04:45
joel: 10m canary results: tolerant reads recovered ~3.2% absolute hit-rate on canary; p95 down ~18ms
tess: widen to 50% while promptlib fix ships
omar: microbenchmark: v3.4.1 reduced opportunistic merge tail by ~6% -> small impact on warmup coalescing
nina: combined contributors: nondeterministic tools serialization (~3-4%) + batcher micro-change (~1-2%) =~ observed drop
joel: next steps: RFC for keyer v4 (include tokenizer sha, promptlib version, canonical tools, sysprompt fingerprint), migration plan
tess: pushing promptlib stableSerialize -> v2.9.1 PR now
metrics-bot: kv-tolerant-read expanded to 50% @05:12
omar: if tolerant_read recovers >3% we keep it 24-48h while rolling canonicalizer
joel: ensure we do NOT write back under alternate key to avoid polluting cache index
nina: will assemble a short blameless writeup for #eng-runtime and file follow-ups in Jira
deploy-bot: workflow kv-tolerant-read-canary completed (50%)
metrics-bot: final canary metrics: tolerant reads netted +2.9% hit-rate and p95 improved ~15ms on canary
nina: thanks team. filing INF-10012 for keyer v4 and INF-10013 for promptlib canonicalizer
tess: note — added CI tests and integration tests for stableSerialize, will notify when release published
joel: opened RFC draft for keyer v4, including spec for tokenizer sha in keys and optional order-insensitive tool hashing
inar: closing thread unless new anomalies crop up. :white_check_mark:
